requirements.title: An input/output control list UNIT= identifies an external or internal unit
requirements.definition: A data transfer statement with an input/output control list includes a UNIT= specifier identifying an external or internal unit, and each data transfer statement identifies an external or internal unit.

pending.control-list-unit-identifies-external-or: Use one external unit opened with NEWUNIT= and one internal character variable, both initialized/filled distinctly, and perform READ/WRITE statements whose UNIT= identifies the intended target; assert the transferred data.
pending.each-data-transfer-identifies-a-unit: For READ, WRITE, and PRINT forms, use positive controls that transfer distinct data through their identified unit; no exhaustive parser claim is made here.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by opening or creating a known file, writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a distinct labelled control path) and then observe only portable properties: successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, exact internal records or values where the source fixes them, named ISO_FORTRAN_ENV status values where the standard names them, or INQUIRE properties fixed by the relevant rule. Processor-dependent unit numbers, filenames except names created by the fixture, storage-unit encodings, buffering, asynchronous timing, IOMSG text, and specific numeric status values are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe that rejection portably; unnumbered program restrictions are not promoted to required diagnostics. IOMSG wording, processor-dependent numeric status values, asynchronous completion timing, and multiple-image or coarray-dependent behavior are never single-image oracles; coarray facets remain out of scope for this suite's fixtures.

requirements.title: Default input and output data-transfer units are processor dependent but tied to * and ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants
requirements.definition: A READ without an input/output control list identifies a processor-dependent unit that is the same as READ(*,...) and INPUT_UNIT; PRINT identifies another processor-dependent unit that is the same as WRITE(*,...) and OUTPUT_UNIT.

pending.default-input-unit-processor-dependent: No portable oracle may require the numeric value of the default input unit; future tests use INPUT_UNIT or harness stdin rather than a literal unit number.
pending.read-star-equals-input-unit: No portable oracle proves unit identity for bare READ, READ(*,...), and READ(INPUT_UNIT,...) rather than merely compatible input effects. An interleaved single-program stdin sequence can show record-order continuity, but 12.5.4 permits a file to be connected to more than one unit as a processor-dependent property and makes I/O through multiple units on the same file processor dependent, so continuity would not distinguish true unit identity from multiple units sharing one input file.
pending.default-output-unit-processor-dependent: No portable oracle may require the numeric value of the default output unit; future tests capture processor output rather than asserting a unit number.
pending.write-star-print-equals-output-unit: No portable oracle proves unit identity for PRINT, WRITE(*,...), and WRITE(OUTPUT_UNIT,...) rather than merely compatible output effects. Interleaving WRITE(OUTPUT_UNIT,'(A)'), WRITE(*,'(A)'), and PRINT '(A)' and asserting captured record order is insufficient: under 12.5.4 a processor may allow one file to be connected to multiple units and the results of I/O through those units are processor dependent, so ordered output could be produced without proving the units are the same.

requirements.title: The identified unit is connected when execution begins
requirements.definition: The unit identified by a data transfer statement shall be connected to a file when execution of the statement begins.

pending.identified-unit-connected-at-execution-b: Positive plans use an internal file or an OPENed external unit before READ/WRITE. A source-control negative attempts transfer on a probed disconnected existing unit, but no required diagnostic or portable runtime result is asserted for this unnumbered restriction.

accounting.rationale: Default-unit processor latitude is split from explicit/equality unit-identification effects.
Processor-dependent choice of default input unit.
READ default unit equality to * and INPUT_UNIT.
Processor-dependent choice of default output unit.
PRINT/WRITE default unit equality to * and OUTPUT_UNIT.
Every data transfer statement identifies a unit.
NOTE only observes that a unit could be preconnected; not normative.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.4-12.6.4.7, execution of a data transfer statement (batch162). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found that the '*', INPUT_UNIT and OUTPUT_UNIT equality facets were planned through stdin/stdout capture and separate controls, which cannot observe unit identity; they are now recorded as having no portable oracle because 12.5.4 makes connecting one file to several units, and I/O through them, processor dependent, and neither NAME= nor NUMBER= rescues it. Source accounting only.
